content: Real wealth consists in having clean water, fresh air, healthy food, and good friends with whom to share them.
author: Alan Watts
sourceWork: The Book: On the Taboo Against Knowing Who You Are (1966)
story:
A former Anglican priest who immersed himself in Eastern philosophy, Alan Watts became a pioneering voice in mid-century California, bridging Taoism, Vedanta, and Zen with Western psychology. Confronting the frantic anxieties of modern consumerism and mechanistic materialism, Watts illuminated the illusion of the separate ego, inviting people to realize they are the entire cosmos experiencing itself.

In formulating this reflection, Alan Watts stripped away superficial conventions to address the core anatomy of real wealth. For Alan Watts, true wisdom is never an abstract luxury, but an urgent practical discipline required to navigate life with clarity and unshakeable dignity.
reflectionPrompt: What would change in your daily outlook if you truly lived by this perspective?
